title: strobe experiment result.json
description: experiments/<exp>/result.json and `strobe bench --json` (SPEC 14.2). Comparisons and refusals are closed; elsewhere strobe may add keys and readers ignore what they do not know. A verdict's words are for people: read verdict_kind and refusal.

id.description: exp_ + 6 hex, or the name bench --id gave.

file_repo.description: The bench file's path in its repository.

decided.description: experiment: every series' primary got a verdict and nothing stopped the bench.

parity.description: check of several targets: the parity matrix, as the text output prints it.

batch.description: check --batch N (SPEC 5.6): run cases shared launches. size: N; launches; cases: the cases they ran; failed_launches: those that failed before a case ran; launch_ms_mean: a launch's own time besides its cases (start, prepare, setup, trace, recording, close), over the launches that ran a case; saved_ms: that time for each case after a launch's first, what a launch per case would have added; unbatched_cases: the cases that ran a launch each because a launch hook of a file without setupKey read ctx.case, ctx.seed or ctx.random(). Null without --batch.

env.description: The device: OS, CPU, GPU, displays, power, strobe's build.

reduced_motion.description: The OS's own reduce-motion setting, read and never changed (Windows animation effects off, macOS Reduce motion, the Linux desktop's enable-animations off): what a target without motion follows. Null when unknown. When true, part of a tracked series' fingerprint for series without motion.

browser.description: The first page target's browser version (each series has its own: series.browser).

gpu.description: The first page target's browser GPU: devices, compositing, software.

window.description: The window's place and size: x, y, width, height.

refresh_hz.description: The display's refresh; null when every series ran headless (no display).

args.description: The command line: command, flags, pos.

plan.description: pin, runs_per_block, aa, looks, alpha, estimate, reserve, gpu_cache, trace (lean, or full: --trace full); seed (the experiment's, --seed or drawn) and used_random (a hook read ctx.seed or called ctx.random(): only then is the seed the workload). A check's plan holds only seed and used_random.

identity.description: What makes two experiments the same comparison (SPEC 14.2).

ledger.description: The other experiments on the same variants (SPEC 14.2).

comparison.description: builds: both sides are builds of one target (an A/B). implementations: each side is a target of its own (SPEC 9.10); every text names the sides by variants[].name, never before/after.

name.description: What reports call this side: the target's name (implementations), else the variant's label.

target.description: implementations: the bench file's target this side runs.

target_kind.description: web, url, app, exe, command, script or native.

engine.description: What the target runs on: metrics of class per_side compare only between sides of one engine.

repo.description: The target's own project (its cwd's strobe.json root), when it is not the bench file's.

process_set.description: The processes the side's metrics summed over, at the last timed block's end: the median count over its blocks and the count per program name.

fixture.description: The bench file's fixture(): one process per block that both sides talk to, outside both process sets (SPEC 9.10).

seed_sha256.description: A hash of the seed folder's paths and contents.

connected.description: Per role: every block's process set held a TCP connection to the fixture's port.

cpu_ms_per_run.description: Per role: the fixture's CPU per measured run, median over blocks (cpu.fixture).

fairness.description: implementations: what both sides shared, as measured.

input.description: os: the sides got OS input (a native side, or a page measured from outside); devtools: two pages driven through DevTools; none: the runs sent no input.

frames.description: Where frames came from on both sides (the OS present source), or null without frames.

gpu_cache.description: os: the OS keeps the GPU shader caches per app where no launch can move them (macOS), shared by both sides.

scoreboard.description: implementations: the journeys' primaries as a family (SPEC 9.10).

family.description: How the count is corrected across journeys (holm).

series.description: One entry per series; bisect: the label of the series it bisects.

stopped.description: Why the bench ended early: its exit code (130 for a stop) and what did not run.

commits.description: bisect: the first-parent line from good to bad (commit, short, subject).

remaining.description: bisect: where the culprit may still be (good, bad).

verdict.description: bisect: found, no change, or unclear.

outcome.description: bisect: what it found, for programs (verdict says it in words).

verdict_kind.description: bisect: good against bad as step 0 found it, or unclear while undecided steps may hide the culprit.

verdictKind.description: untested: a secondary the gate did not test (shown as —); descriptive: shown, never decided (·). A leak verdict: worse leaks, same does not grow or levels off.

hidden.description: WindowHidden: how the window was hidden.

sampling.description: A JavaScript sampler (SPEC 8.3): the interval asked and the median gap it kept between samples of the page's main thread, in µs, and how many gaps that median is of.

comparison.description: One metric, base against head over the pairs (SPEC 9.3).

estimate.description: Relative change when relative, else head minus base in the metric's unit.

bound.description: The equivalence bound (or the no-worse margin), in the comparison's scale.

better.description: The direction it counted as better: the metric's, or for a metric.<name> the one its command's lines gave. Absent in older results (readers: stats::better_in).

words.description: Its words for the better and worse directions (faster, slower; more, less for a metric.<name> better higher).

refusal.description: When verdict_kind is refused: the validator and why.

across.description: implementations: the metric's comparability class (SPEC 7.1); per_side never reaches a comparison (refused NotComparable when declared).

care_note.description: across care: what the number sums on each side, printed wherever it is.

p_repeated.description: implementations, primary: the p-value adjusted for the series' sequential looks.

holm_decided.description: implementations, primary: still decided after Holm across the journeys.

perSide.description: implementations: a per_side metric's blocks on one side: their median and the median's own interval over them (order statistics, stats::median_interval). Never compared.

leakPrimary.description: A leak series' primary: the head's growth verdict.

checkPrimary.description: A --check series' primary: only its name, since nothing is compared.

blocksPrimary.description: A bench --blocks series' primary: its name, and a refusal when the blocks cannot give it a value (TailTooShort, NoPhase, a block's refusal).

gapPrimary.description: implementations: a journey one side cannot run (a parity gap): its primary, refused ParityGap, with nothing compared.

overhead.description: What strobe cost inside the measured runs, as % of one core (SPEC 19); a series holds its blocks' mean.

sampler_pct.description: The OS and GPU sampler's thread (budget 0.5%).

reserve_pct.description: The reserved-CPU sweep (budget 5%, on strobe's own CPUs).

terminal_pct.description: A tty() target's terminal reader: reading, parsing and answering the program's output (budget 0.5%).

pixel_pct.description: strobe's pixel reads inside the runs (captures and image matching for image locators and pixel waits, opening the window's capture and decoding a template included), CPU as % of the runs' wall time (budget 0.5%; over 2% refuses timing and latency metrics).

encoder_pct.description: A filmed block's (--video) video encoder process, its CPU over the video's span as % of one core. No budget: a filmed block is never timed.

step.description: One bisect step: the experiment of commit against good, summarized.

kind.description: runs, launch or leak; check (--check), pixels (--pixels-only), blocks (--blocks: one build's timed blocks, nothing compared).

headless.description: A page target ran in a headless browser (--headless, or the target's headless): no display, so its frame, input-to-screen latency, scroll, canvas and GPU-use metrics are refused (Headless); CPU, counters, memory and input pacing stay.

engine.description: A page target's browser engine (--engine, or the target's engine).

input.description: The input devices the series' pages saw (each block keeps its own). desktop: a fine pointer that hovers, nothing coarse, no touch, which a page target sees unless it emulates a device, headless too (checked before setup: DeviceMismatch); a page target with emulate: "mobile" sees touch and one with emulate: "touch" hybrid, checked the same way; an app's page (Electron, a webview, a command's browser) sees the machine's: hybrid (a fine pointer with touch beside it), touch (no fine pointer), none (no pointer at all). Sides that saw different ones are refused (VariantMismatch). Part of a page series' tracked fingerprint. Null without a page, and in results from before strobe recorded it.

browser.description: The browser versions this series' blocks ran (`a / b` when the sides of an implementation comparison ran two); part of a tracked series' fingerprint.

emulate.description: What the series' page target emulates (its `emulate`): a phone or a touch screen; null for a desktop. Part of a tracked series' fingerprint.

mobile.description: bench --mobile: the adb serial of the phone (or emulator) whose Chrome ran the series' phone target, its own screen and touch, nothing emulated; its blocks' recordings keep the phone (meta.json phone). Null otherwise.

display.description: Linux native series: where the app showed its windows, the session's X server or the headless Wayland compositor strobe started per launch (frames and input latency refused Headless); null for other targets and OSes. Part of a tracked series' fingerprint (native_display) and the rerun ledger's identity (displays).

motion.description: The series' target's `motion`: reduce (the page or app prefers reduced motion, set in strobe's launch alone; a page was checked with matchMedia before setup, a native app took its profile's declared motion.reduce); null: the OS's own setting (env.reduced_motion). Part of a tracked series' fingerprint and the rerun ledger's identity.

window.description: The window the series drew in, as reports print it: `1400×900`, `390×844 @3x · emulated mobile`, `1400×900 · reduced motion` (its blocks' content area, else the window it asked for). Null without a window, for a series refused before it ran, and in an implementation comparison (see fairness.window).

windowless.description: Every target the series runs opens no window (a script, a command line, an app with window: false).

href.description: A url() target's address: the page both sides load whatever their build (a series of builds of one is refused VariantMismatch before anything builds).

untimed.description: What ctx.untimed left out of the series' runs (SPEC 9.6): stretches a run and ms of each run, each the median over its blocks of the blocks' median per run (`untimed.n`, `untimed.ms` in a block's values); null when no run left one out.

pass.description: A series that counts cpu.instructions apart from its times (Linux perf events never run in a timing block, SPEC 7.5): the other kind's blocks and pairs. counters: whether these are the counter blocks (cpu.instructions is read from them, every other metric from blocks); else they are the timing blocks and blocks hold cpu.instructions. Null otherwise.

until.description: A launch series: what each launch was timed until. end is visible, painted or settled (the window), milestone (with milestone, its name), state (with state: a tty() program's own state on its STROBE_EVENTS stream) or selector (with selector, the case's until). Null for other series; absent in older results (readers then infer it from the launches' values).

stopped.description: Why the series ended: primary decided, max pairs, max time, …

primary_pairs.description: The pairs the primary's verdict, estimate and interval come from: the look that decided it, fewer than pairs when the series ran on for its secondaries or family. Absent in older results (then pairs).

warmup_values.description: The discarded warm-up blocks' primary value per side (base, head; SPEC 9.1); null for a resumed series.

steps.description: Mean wall time per step of a block, in order.

same.description: implementations: what each expect.same element read, by its name: { setup, run[], reset[] }.

ops.description: implementations: the measured runs' input calls, each call's median count per run (a typed character each).

directions.description: cli() targets: the direction each metric.<name> is better in, as the command's lines said.

reduced_motion.description: Page blocks: whether the page matched (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), read with its input devices before setup. Sides that read differently are refused VariantMismatch. Absent without a page and in older results.

attribution.description: The attribution recording per variant (check: the one recording).

attribution_sampling.description: The attribution recordings' page sampler (SPEC 8.3): check, the one recording's; a comparison, per variant (a side without one is left out); null when none sampled a page. Absent in older results.

shown.description: What was on screen (SPEC 10.2): base and head (each with its first block's thumb_start and thumb_end as data URLs), changed (builds only).

pixels.description: --pixels: per snapshot, whether base and head drew the same pixels.

video.description: --video (SPEC 8.8): the recordings that hold each side's video (video.json beside it), and mixed when their kinds differ.

leak.description: A leak series: growth verdicts per variant (js_heap, dom_nodes or native_host, each with verdict and verdict_kind).

declared.description: check: the metrics the case declared.

actions.description: check: the actions of a case without a recording (it failed, or its kind keeps none): path (<case>.actions.json.gz, or failed-<case>.actions.json.gz, beside result.json, owner-only), count, and failed. strobe query <exp> actions reads them.

batch_id.description: check --batch: the launch that ran the case (from 1); cases of one launch share its recording, whose meta.json batch lists them.

batch_seq.description: check --batch: the case's place in its launch (from 1): the first ran cold, the others after the cases before them.

batch_note.description: check --batch: the case after this one did not find the screen it expects after this case's reset, and ran in a fresh launch; or this case's launch hook read what differs per case (a file without setupKey), so it ran alone and the cases that would have shared its launch ran a launch each.

hero.description: implementations: the case says hero: true.

targets.description: implementations: the target each side ran (base, head).

target_kinds.description: implementations: each side's target kind (base, head).

adapted.description: implementations: steps means the case gives each target its own run (run: { <target>: fn }); null: one run through each side's ui.

equivalence.description: implementations: each expect.same element, what both sides read at the end of the journey in the last pair, whether every pair agreed, and how many pairs were read.

journey.description: check: the case and its params, whatever target ran it (a row of the parity matrix).

same.description: check: what each expect.same element read ({ setup, run[], reset[] }), as blocks keep it.

ops.description: check: the run's input calls (call -> count), as blocks keep them.

journey_refusal.description: check: why this target's journey is not the first target's (NotEquivalent, InputMismatch).

per_side.description: implementations: per_side metrics per role, never compared.

gap.description: implementations: a journey one side cannot run (a parity gap): nothing ran, its primary is refused ParityGap.
